name: WA-02
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+12 district with a long-serving incumbent, Rick Larsen, seeking another term
Overwhelming financial asymmetry: Larsen raised $2.55M versus about $9K for Edwin Feller
Prediction markets price Larsen's win probability near 96 percent
No public general-election polling or expert ratings to challenge the fundamentals
model.rationale: Every available signal points the same way: the district's twelve-point Democratic lean, Larsen's incumbency, a roughly 280-to-1 fundraising gap, and markets pricing this near a 96 percent Democratic win. With no polls or ratings suggesting otherwise, the fundamentals support a comfortable Larsen margin.
model.watch: A late surge of independent spending backing Feller, or fresh polling showing the race far tighter than fundamentals imply, would be the main reason to revisit this forecast.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Washington's 2nd District leans Democratic by twelve points, and Rick Larsen has held the seat since 2001. He enters the general election with an enormous financial advantage, having raised about $2.55 million to Edwin Feller's roughly $9,000, and outside spending in the race has been negligible. Prediction markets put Larsen's chances near 96 percent.

No public general-election polling is available, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, the incumbency edge, and the resource gap. Those factors all point in the same direction, suggesting a comfortable margin for Larsen. Feller would need an outside shock, such as heavy independent spending or a sharp shift in the national environment, to make the race competitive. As it stands, the district's lean and the campaign's asymmetry make this one of the safer Democratic holds in the Pacific Northwest.
